heading: Theorem 9.1.
context: \textbf{Theorem 9.1.} A smooth almost complex structure is induced by a complex coordinate atlas if and only if its tensor \eqref{courseIII:almost-complex-structures-and-integrability:eq:1.5} vanishes.

heading: Theorem 2.1.
context: \textbf{Theorem 2.1.} There is a smooth function \(F\), equal to \(f\) outside a compact subset of \(U\), with no critical points in the region where the two given critical points and their connecting trajectory are changed. No new critical points occur anywhere. There is a smooth interpolation from \(f\) to \(F\), fixed outside that same region.

heading: Proof: finite covers.
context: **Proof: finite covers.** A bundle trivial on one open set satisfies all assertions by Proposition 6.1. Suppose they hold over \(U,V,U\cap V\). The two degree-\(r\) Thom classes agree on the intersection, because they have the same fibre values. Relative Mayer–Vietoris gives a common class on \(U\cup V\), uniquely since \(H^{r-1}(E_{U\cap V},(E_{U\cap V})_0)=0\). It still has the required fibre values.

heading: Proof: passage to arbitrary bases.
context: **Proof: passage to arbitrary bases.** For each compact subset \(C\subset B\), the restricted bundle has a finite trivializing cover. Denote its Thom class by \(u_C\). If \(C\subset D\), uniqueness shows that \(u_D\) restricts to \(u_C\).

heading: Proposition 8.1.
context: **Proposition 8.1.** If a positive-rank oriented bundle has a nowhere-zero section, its Euler class is zero. The same conclusion holds for the mod-two Euler class without orientation.
